input.description: Rename disableTooltip to hideHint in feature-1 to feature-20
input.prompt:
We are renaming one Angular component input across a codebase. Context: `PillComponent` (selector `app-pill`, file src/app/lib/pill.component.ts) had an input `disableTooltip`, now renamed to `hideHint` (already done in the lib files — do not touch src/app/lib/*.ts, src/styles.css, or src/app/app.component.ts, those are already correctly updated). `FancyPillComponent` (selector `app-fancy-pill`) and `StatusPillComponent` (selector `app-status-pill`) both `extends PillComponent` and inherit this same input — their usages must also be renamed.

HOWEVER, two unrelated components happen to have their OWN input with the identical old name `disableTooltip`, which must NOT be renamed: `CardComponent` (selector `app-card`) and `PillLegacyComponent` (selector `app-pill-legacy`). input.prompt:
We are renaming one Angular component input across a codebase. Context: `PillComponent` (selector `app-pill`, file src/app/lib/pill.component.ts) had an input `disableTooltip`, now renamed to `hideHint` (already done in the lib files — do not touch src/app/lib/*.ts, src/styles.css, or src/app/app.component.ts, those are already correctly updated). `FancyPillComponent` (selector `app-fancy-pill`) and `StatusPillComponent` (selector `app-status-pill`) both `extends PillComponent` and inherit this same input — their usages must also be renamed.

HOWEVER, two unrelated components happen to have their OWN input with the identical old name `disableTooltip`, which must NOT be renamed: `CardComponent` (selector `app-card`) and `PillLegacyComponent` (selector `app-pill-legacy`). Also, many of the "feature" screen components have their own unrelated class field literally named `disableTooltip` (e.g. `disableTooltip = true;`) — this must also NOT be renamed, nor any plain/bare read of it like `@if (disableTooltip)` or `this.disableTooltip` (when there is no `.` receiver that is a pill/fancy-pill/status-pill reference). Comments and descriptive text mentioning the word "disableTooltip" must never be changed either.

Your job: apply this rename inside the following files only (edit both the .ts and .html file in each directory, if both exist and contain the string "disableTooltip" — some directories may only have one of the two, or the word in a file that doesn't need any change, that's fine, just check with grep first):

src/app/features/feature-81/

src/app/features/feature-83/
src/app/features/feature-84/
src/app/features/feature-85/
src/app/features/feature-86/

src/app/features/feature-100/

(each directory has a `feature-N.component.ts` and possibly a `feature-N.component.html`; some use an inline `template:` string in the .ts file instead of an external .html file)

Precise rules to decide, for each occurrence of the literal text "disableTooltip" in these files:

RULE A — attribute form inside an element tag's opening (between the tag name and the tag's closing `>`), either bound `[disableTooltip]="expr"` (or with single quotes) or bare/plain `disableTooltip` with no value:
  - If the enclosing tag is `<app-pill`, `<app-fancy-pill`, or `<app-status-pill` → RENAME to `hideHint` (i.e. `[hideHint]="expr"` or bare `hideHint`). This applies even if the tag spans multiple lines and the attribute is on a line after the opening tag name, as long as no `>` has closed that tag yet.
  - If the enclosing tag is `<app-card` or `<app-pill-legacy` → DO NOT RENAME, leave exactly as-is.

RULE B — member-access form reading the input off a component reference, e.g. `someRef.disableTooltip()` in a template or in TypeScript (no parens for PillLegacyComponent, but that one is never renamed anyway):
  - Find how `someRef` is declared, in the SAME file: either a template reference variable `#someRef` written on an `<app-pill>`, `<app-fancy-pill>`, or `<app-status-pill>` tag, or a `viewChild(...)`/`@ViewChild(...)`/`viewChildren(...)` in the TS class typed to `PillComponent`/`FancyPillComponent`/`StatusPillComponent` (check the generic type argument or the component class passed in), or an array/signal of one of those three component types that then gets `.filter(x => x.disableTooltip())` or similar called on it.
  - If `someRef` resolves to `PillComponent`/`FancyPillComponent`/`StatusPillComponent` → RENAME the call to `.hideHint()`.
  - If `someRef` resolves to `CardComponent` (e.g. a `#someRef` declared on `<app-card>`) or `PillLegacyComponent` → DO NOT RENAME.

RULE C — a bare `disableTooltip` identifier with no `.` receiver and not inside a tag's attribute list (e.g. `@if (disableTooltip)`, `this.disableTooltip`, a field declaration `disableTooltip = true;`, or inside a comment or a plain string/text) → this is always the screen component's own unrelated field or just descriptive text → NEVER RENAME, leave exactly as-is.

input.prompt:
We are renaming one Angular component input across a codebase. Context: `PillComponent` (selector `app-pill`, file src/app/lib/pill.component.ts) had an input `disableTooltip`, now renamed to `hideHint` (already done in the lib files — do not touch src/app/lib/*.ts, src/styles.css, or src/app/app.component.ts, those are already correctly updated). `FancyPillComponent` (selector `app-fancy-pill`) and `StatusPillComponent` (selector `app-status-pill`) both `extends PillComponent` and inherit this same input — their usages must also be renamed.

HOWEVER, two unrelated components happen to have their OWN input with the identical old name `disableTooltip`, which must NOT be renamed: `CardComponent` (selector `app-card`) and `PillLegacyComponent` (selector `app-pill-legacy`). Also, many of the "feature" screen components have their own unrelated class field literally named `disableTooltip` (e.g. `disableTooltip = true;`) — this must also NOT be renamed, nor any plain/bare read of it like `@if (disableTooltip)` or `this.disableTooltip` (when there is no `.` receiver that is a pill/fancy-pill/status-pill reference). Comments and descriptive text mentioning the word "disableTooltip" must never be changed either.

Your job: apply this rename inside the following files only (edit both the .ts and .html file in each directory, if both exist and contain the string "disableTooltip" — some directories may only have one of the two, or the word in a file that doesn't need any change, that's fine, just check with grep first):

(each directory has a `feature-N.component.ts` and possibly a `feature-N.component.html`; some use an inline `template:` string in the .ts file instead of an external .html file)

Precise rules to decide, for each occurrence of the literal text "disableTooltip" in these files:

RULE A — attribute form inside an element tag's opening (between the tag name and the tag's closing `>`), either bound `[disableTooltip]="expr"` (or with single quotes) or bare/plain `disableTooltip` with no value:
  - If the enclosing tag is `<app-pill`, `<app-fancy-pill`, or `<app-status-pill` → RENAME to `hideHint` (i.e. `[hideHint]="expr"` or bare `hideHint`). This applies even if the tag spans multiple lines and the attribute is on a line after the opening tag name, as long as no `>` has closed that tag yet.
  - If the enclosing tag is `<app-card` or `<app-pill-legacy` → DO NOT RENAME, leave exactly as-is.

RULE B — member-access form reading the input off a component reference, e.g. `someRef.disableTooltip()` in a template or in TypeScript (no parens for PillLegacyComponent, but that one is never renamed anyway):
  - Find how `someRef` is declared, in the SAME file: either a template reference variable `#someRef` written on an `<app-pill>`, `<app-fancy-pill>`, or `<app-status-pill>` tag, or a `viewChild(...)`/`@ViewChild(...)`/`viewChildren(...)` in the TS class typed to `PillComponent`/`FancyPillComponent`/`StatusPillComponent` (check the generic type argument or the component class passed in), or an array/signal of one of those three component types that then gets `.filter(x => x.disableTooltip())` or similar called on it.
  - If `someRef` resolves to `PillComponent`/`FancyPillComponent`/`StatusPillComponent` → RENAME the call to `.hideHint()`.
